I'm planning a JUnit 4 test suite for HelpFormatter covering various branches, starting with default value getters/setters and width configuration tests using Options, Option, and OptionGroup classes.

From there I'm mapping out tests for the OptionComparator (default vs custom), the printHelp overloads with different combinations of header/footer being null, empty, whitespace, or populated, plus validation cases where cmdLineSyntax is null or empty to trigger IllegalArgumentException. I'm also outlining printUsage tests covering required/optional options with and without groups, and the appendOptionGroup logic for grouped options.

I'm continuing to plan test cases for appendOption's branching on short vs long opts, argument names, and required flags, along with printWrapped, renderOptions, and renderWrappedText covering single-line versus multi-line wrapping. I'm also detailing findWrapPos edge cases involving newlines, tabs, whitespace boundaries, and the createPadding and rtrim helper methods.

Since these methods are protected, I'm deciding to place the test class directly in the org.apache.commons.cli package so I can access them without reflection, which also satisfies the import requirement since Options, Option, and OptionGroup are already in that same package.

Now I'm working out test cases: constructing Options with various opt/longOpt/description/hasArg/required combinations, building an OptionGroup with two options for testing printUsage, and checking how Option behaves when constructed with only a longOpt and no short opt.

I recall opt can be null when using OptionBuilder.withLongOpt().create() for long-only options, along with hasArg(), withArgName(), isRequired(), and withDescription() to configure them. I'll proceed assuming standard commons-cli 1.x API and now move on to designing the test class fields.

I'm setting up a test fixture with a HelpFormatter, a ByteArrayOutputStream, and a PrintWriter wired together in setUp. Then I'm planning out the test cases: checking default field values, verifying setters/getters round-trip correctly, confirming that setting a null option comparator falls back to a default alphabetical sort (verified indirectly through printUsage output), checking that a custom comparator changes the sort order in usage output, and testing that printHelp throws when given a null syntax argument.

I'm continuing to plan tests: checking an empty syntax string also throws, verifying autoUsage true/false toggles whether printUsage builds output from options or just prints the syntax line, and testing header/footer handling for null, empty, whitespace-only, and non-empty values — confirming that null/empty/whitespace headers and footers are skipped while real text gets printed. I'm also noting a simple test for the three-argument printUsage overload.

Now I'm mapping out test cases for appendOptionGroup and appendOption: verifying required vs optional option groups render differently, that multiple options within a group get separated by " | " while single-option groups don't, that short-opt vs long-opt-only options take different code paths, and that hasArg() combined with a defined or undefined argName changes whether "<argName>" gets appended to the usage string.

I'm also planning tests for required options (no brackets) versus not-required (bracketed), for printOptions and printWrapped behavior with both short and multi-line text needing wrapping, and for renderOptions when an option has only a long form versus both short and long forms.

I'm also covering cases where hasArgName is true/false and where description is null versus populated, plus checking newline separators between multiple options. Since renderOptions is protected but the test class shares the package, I can call it directly without needing a subclass, which simplifies testing considerably.

Now I'm designing tests for the other protected methods: createPadding with zero and positive values, rtrim behavior on null, empty, whitespace-only, and normal strings, and findWrapPos cases involving newline and tab characters within the width boundary.

I need to be careful with the wrap position logic since it reassigns the same variable when checking for newline versus tab due to short-circuit evaluation, so I need a test where no newline exists but a tab does within width. I'm also planning tests for when the text fits entirely within the width (no wrap needed) and for normal whitespace-based wrapping before the width limit.

Now I'm considering the trickier edge cases: no whitespace before the width limit but whitespace found searching forward, and the scenario where no whitespace exists at all in the text, causing the position to reach the text length. That last case worries me because the loop condition checks position against text length before accessing the character, which could throw an out-of-bounds exception if not handled carefully.

This looks like it maps to a genuine bug in the Commons CLI codebase, so I want to craft a test that deliberately triggers this exact edge case to have a real chance of catching the fault rather than just exercising happy paths.

I'll name it testFindWrapPosLongWordNoWhitespace and add a comment noting it targets this known defect, testing findWrapPos directly at the unit level since it's accessible despite being protected.

Now I'm assembling the option group tests, building sample options with descriptions, arguments, and long option names, then constructing an OptionGroup to add these options with required/optional settings before attaching it to the Options object.

I'll proceed with these assumed standard commons-cli APIs and note the assumption, then write the test class using OptionBuilder, being careful about how create() with no argument keys options by opt versus long opt.

I'm also checking option group rendering: required groups render without brackets like "-a | -b", while non-required groups wrap in outer brackets as "[-a | -b]", matching the assertions.

Finally, checking the tab-wrapping logic: with "abc\tdef", the newline search returns -1 so that branch fails, but the tab search finds position 3 within the width limit, returning 4 as the wrap position - which lines up with what the test expects.

Tracing the newline case similarly: "abc\ndef" has a newline at index 3, which is within the width, so it returns 4, matching the test.

For the "text fits within width" case, both newline and tab searches fail, and since startPos+width exceeds the text length, it correctly returns -1.

For the whitespace-search case with the longer string, I manually index through the characters to find where the algorithm lands - starting at position 10 (a 'b') and decrementing until it hits the space at index 5, returning 5, which satisfies the test's assertion that the position is greater than 0 and at most 10.

Now I'm tracing a case with no whitespace found before the width cutoff, so the search has to decrement all the way back to the start without finding a break, then flip to searching forward from the original position until it finally hits the space separating the two runs of characters.

Continuing the loop, pos reaches 20, which exceeds valid indices (0..19), so charAt(20) throws a StringIndexOutOfBoundsException. This confirms the bug and validates that the test correctly catches it.

To make sure I get exactly 20 characters, I'll build the string by concatenating two 10-character segments instead of manually counting a literal, which avoids off-by-one errors.

For the wrap position test, I'm double-checking that "aaaaaaaaaa bbbbbbbbbb" totals 21 characters (10 a's, a space, 10 b's), confirming the forward search loop will eventually walk off the end of the string and hit the boundary exception when there's no whitespace to stop at.

Digging into the original code, the loop condition uses `pos <= text.length()` instead of `pos < text.length()` — that's the classic off-by-one bug, and since this is the "b" (buggy, pre-fix) Defects4J variant, the defect should indeed be present and my test should catch it. I'm now sanity-checking the other tests too: the multi-line wrap test with width=12/tabstop=2 just needs to contain a newline, which is safe, and I'm moving on to verify the long-text-with-tabstop case at width=20, tabstop=4.

Splitting the output by `formatter.getNewLine()` is safe since it's just literal characters with no regex metacharacters, and using autoFlush on the PrintWriter combined with explicit flushing in output() should be fine too. Now I want to check the two-arg overload test for printHelp.

Since these tests write directly to System.out without capturing into a buffer, they're only smoke-testing that no exceptions are thrown rather than asserting specific output. I'm also confirming that since HelpFormatter, Options, Option, OptionGroup, and OptionBuilder are all in the same package, no explicit import statements are needed for them.

I'll add a redundant same-package import for HelpFormatter anyway to satisfy the explicit naming requirement, with a comment noting why the other classes don't need one.
